statement: An editing tool may write a Unicode escape as the character it names: check the bytes after writing any escape for a line terminator or blank, and in a regex prefer an ASCII-only form. 2026-11-10, cejel #550, my own near miss. Rewriting sixteen ^\s*X literals, I wrote the class [^\S\n\r\u2028\u2029] through the agent's edit tool; the file received the raw U+2028 and U+2029 characters, which end a regex literal in JavaScript, so every rewritten literal was cut at \r. Typecheck was not run yet; the ReDoS guard caught it only because it compiles each literal and counted the SyntaxError as a failure (399 failures). NBSP was converted the same way; \u0085 was not. The fix was a form with no escape at all: (?:(?=.)\s), a blank that . also matches, so no line terminator; string literals took the \u{2028} form, which the tool left as text. A grep for the raw characters over the changed files then returned only files the change did not touch.
